data.mechanism: Ragulator does two jobs on the Rags. It tethers the Rag heterodimer to the lysosomal surface, and it acts as an unusual exchange factor: first reported as a GEF for RagA/B (BAR2012), its exchange activity was later placed on RagC, where releasing GTP unlocks the inactive state (SHE2018B). Loading RagA with GTP is done by arginine-bound SLC38A9 (see SLC38A9-RAG).
data.mechanism_beginner: Ragulator anchors the Rag proteins to the lysosome and also helps flip them into their "on" shape, together with a second protein, SLC38A9. Both jobs are shown in biochemical experiments.
data.boundary: Human cells, Drosophila and purified recombinant proteins (BAR2012, SAN2010, SHE2018B). The exchange activity was first assigned to RagA/B and later to RagC, so the exact step is still being refined. Whole-animal and human relevance are not tested here.
